target.name: Bay of Bengal Cyclone to Kandy Floods

citations.label: NASA-ISRO SAR (NISAR) & Copernicus Sentinel-1
citations.text: L-band & C-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) backscatter observations provided via NASA ASF DAAC and ESA Copernicus.

citations.label: NASA Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM IMERG)
citations.text: Half-hourly multi-satellite precipitation estimates from the NASA GPM Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for GPM (IMERG).

citations.label: NASA MERRA-2 Atmospheric Reanalysis
citations.text: Surface wind speed and vector fields from the Modern-Era Retrospective analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2.

citations.text: Multi-spectral high-resolution optical surface reflectance and Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI).

region_label: Bay of Bengal -> Kandy, Sri Lanka

story_scenes.title: Bay of Bengal Low Forms
story_scenes.narration: Warm +29.4°C waters in the southwest Bay of Bengal feed a tightening 996 hPa low-pressure depression 440 km east of Sri Lanka, spinning up maritime trade gusts.
story_scenes.why_these_layers: Ocean surface temperature + surface wind reveal the thermal fuel and early vortex rotation before landfall.
story_scenes.illusion_note: Radar is still quiet on land; atmospheric datasets spot the disaster 48 hours earlier.

causal_chain.explanation: Warm ocean evaporation lowers central air pressure and builds latent moisture.

story_scenes.title: Cyclonic Wind Corridor
story_scenes.narration: Cyclonic inflow accelerates to 18.8 m/s (68 km/h) across eastern Sri Lanka, funneling a river of tropical moisture straight toward the Central Highlands.
story_scenes.why_these_layers: Wind vectors + GPM rainfall track exactly where ocean moisture is steered into inland hills.
story_scenes.illusion_note: High wind speeds (>8 m/s) trigger early capillary wave roughening along reservoirs.

causal_chain.explanation: Tight pressure gradient accelerates wet air inland toward the highlands.
Steep mountain topography forces warm moist air upward, condensing heavy rain.

story_scenes.title: Kandy Cloudburst Blinds Cameras
story_scenes.narration: Stalled storm cells unload 54 mm/hr over Kandy while an 88% thick cloud deck blinds regular sunlight cameras—making all-weather SAR radar essential.
story_scenes.why_these_layers: Showing GPM rainfall beside blinded optical cameras proves why microwave SAR must take over.
story_scenes.illusion_note: Cloud Blanking triggers on Sentinel-2 optical, leaving only SAR able to map rising river banks.

causal_chain.explanation: Thick cumulonimbus tops block visible sunlight while saturating mountain soil.

story_scenes.title: Flood Surge & Wind-Ripple Fix
story_scenes.narration: Sentinel-1 & NISAR pierce storm clouds to reveal -24 dB flooded Mahaweli valleys and slope slips. AI Wind Guard strips out 14.6 m/s wave glare over Victoria Reservoir so floodwater isn't hidden.
story_scenes.why_these_layers: SAR sees surface water & hillslope slips while MERRA-2 wind identifies choppy wave illusions.
story_scenes.illusion_note: Radar Illusion Guard: removes +13.5 dB wind-ripple backscatter false negatives over water.

causal_chain.explanation: Smooth standing floodwater bounces radar away like a dark mirror through clouds.
Choppy reservoir ripples scatter radar back, tricking single-sensor water detectors.

story_scenes.title: Power Blackouts & Drainage
story_scenes.narration: Flooded substations plunge Kandy districts into a 78% NASA Black Marble blackout before waters slowly recede and emergency power restoration begins.
story_scenes.why_these_layers: Combining SAR water persistence with Black Marble nightlights prioritizes neighborhoods still without power.
story_scenes.illusion_note: Wind eases below 4 m/s, restoring calm mirror backscatter across receding channels.

causal_chain.explanation: Submerged transformers and landslide-cut distribution lines knock out city grid sectors.

illusion_summary: 15 m/s cyclonic wind gusts whip waves across Victoria Reservoir & flooded plains, spiking SAR backscatter by +13 dB so raw radar falsely reads floodwater as dry land. Cross-checking MERRA-2 wind restores the hidden water.
causal_summary: Sea-Level Low Pressure (996 hPa, Bay of Bengal) -> SW/NE Monsoon Wind Jet (18.8 m/s, +18h) -> Orographic Cloudburst over Kandy (54 mm/hr, +36h) -> Valley Flood & Slope Slips (-24 dB SAR, +48h) -> Urban Grid Blackout (-78% Black Marble, +54h).

geo_features.label: Bay of Bengal Low Pressure (996 hPa)
geo_features.detail: Warm sea surface (+29.4°C) intensifies deep atmospheric convection and cyclonic inflow.

geo_features.label: Cyclonic Moisture & Wind Track
geo_features.detail: 18.8 m/s easterly/northeasterly jet funnels ocean moisture into Kandy Highlands over 36 hours.

geo_features.label: Orographic Cloudburst Core (185 mm/day)
geo_features.detail: GPM IMERG measures peak 54 mm/hr stalling against Knuckles & Peradeniya ridges.

geo_features.label: Mahaweli & Katugastota SAR Floodplain
geo_features.detail: Sentinel-1 VV drops from -9.5 dB to -24.1 dB across 1,420 ha of inundated valley settlements.

geo_features.label: Victoria Reservoir Wind-Ripple Illusion
geo_features.detail: 14.6 m/s gusts create capillary waves (+13.5 dB raw SAR spike); AI Wind Guard restores true water mask.

geo_features.label: Peradeniya–Hanthana Slope Coherence Loss
geo_features.detail: Interferometric coherence drops below 0.22 on saturated 28° hillslopes.

geo_features.label: Kandy Urban Power Grid Blackout (-78%)
geo_features.detail: NASA Black Marble VNP46A2 plunges from 42.5 to 9.2 nW/cm²/sr during peak river surge.
